title: QBR: Two-Track Outcome + Technical Review (standard & enterprise)
summary: A pragmatic QBR deck template that runs two parallel review tracks (Outcome & Technical Health) with a unified renewal decision framework and an integrated renewal tracker. Designed to scale from small standard accounts to large enterprise engagements.
content:
Purpose: Provide a reproducible QBR structure that surface business outcomes, usage economics (cost-per-inference), and technical health signals so CS + Solutions + Product can align on a renewal recommendation. This doc contains: slide-by-slide template, speaker notes, a lightweight renewal tracker table, risk scoring rubric, and a post-QBR runbook for actions and owners.

Audience: Customer success manager (owner), solutions engineer (technical co-owner), account executive (commercial context) and customer stakeholders (product, infra, finance).

Format overview: Two-track QBR run in a single meeting (60–90m):
 - Track A — Outcome & Business Metrics (30–40m): usage trends, feature adoption, ROI signals, executive asks.
 - Track B — Technical Health & Ops (25–40m): latency/cost SLOs, model accuracy/regressions, incident review, roadmap impacts.
 - Closing — Renewal recommendation + next 90-day plan (10–15m).

Slide 1: Title + meeting meta
 - Title: QBR — [Customer name] | Two-Track Review (Outcome + Technical)
 - Subtitle: Period: [MM/YYYY – MM/YYYY] • Owner: [CSM name] • Co-host: [SE name]
 - Speaker note: Set expectations for split structure, ask for executive sponsor to confirm priority items at the start.

Slide 2: Executive one-pager (90s)
 - Top-line: Renewal posture (On-track / At-risk / Upsell candidate), Net $ impact (ARR delta), Primary success metrics (2–3).
 - Quick wins and outstanding blockers (bulleted).
 - Speaker note: Start with the decision — frame whether we're recommending renewal and high-level rationale.

Track A (Outcome & Business Metrics)
Slide 3: Usage & Adoption snapshot
 - Charts: Monthly active users (MAU) using Redwood-powered features, requests per minute, top 5 endpoints by volume.
 - Adoption notes: New teams onboarded, feature flags toggled on.
 - Speaker note: Call out where adoption lags behind expectations and any gating product feedback.

Slide 4: Value delivered — business KPIs
 - Show 2–3 customer business KPIs tied to Redwood (example: chat-response completion rate, avg time-to-answer, end-user NPS lift, revenue enablement metrics).
 - Annotate the causal link and confidence level.
 - Speaker note: Be explicit about assumptions and data sources.

Slide 5: Economics & cost-per-inference analysis
 - Table: Token volume, avg tokens / request, unit cost (hosted/dedicated), estimated monthly cost, cost per active user.
 - Callouts: opportunities for batching, caching, or quantization recommendations to lower unit cost.
 - Speaker note: Provide a concrete opt-in change (e.g., enable prefix caching) and estimated savings.

Slide 6: Roadmap impact & feature asks
 - List product roadmap items that affect customer outcomes and a RAG (red/amber/green) status for each.
 - Dependencies and estimated ship dates.
 - Speaker note: Align on priority and ask for a customer decision where needed.

Track B (Technical Health & Ops)
Slide 7: SLA & performance review
 - Metrics: p95/p99 latency by endpoint, error rates, throttling events, capacity incidents.
 - Comparison vs. target SLOs.
 - Speaker note: If p99 breaches occurred, describe mitigation and long-term fix.

Slide 8: Model quality & regression guardrails
 - Metrics: classification accuracy / hallucination incidents / rerank precision (per monitored prompt set), drift indicators.
 - Recent evals: prompt set A/B comparisons, examples of regressions and mitigations.
 - Speaker note: Recommend a rollback buffer or canary schedule if model variants are volatile.

Slide 9: Operational health — tooling & pipelines
 - Items: KV/prefix cache hit rates, batching efficiency, autoscale events, infra cost anomalies.
 - Actionable items: enable autoscaling window, increase burst capacity, request Dedicated pool sizing change.
 - Speaker note: Translate ops signals into customer-visible risk statements.

Slide 10: Security, compliance & data handling
 - Summary of audit items, key management status, private deployment considerations (if applicable).
 - Any open SOC/pen test items and dates.
 - Speaker note: For enterprise customers, make this a prioritized agenda item.

Slide 11: Incident retrospective (if any)
 - Brief chronology, customer impact, root cause, corrective actions, and timeline for remediation.
 - Speaker note: Keep to facts, avoid jargon, and ensure action owners are named.

Closing & Recommendation
Slide 12: Renewal posture & recommended path
 - Options: Renew as-is (standard), Renew + Dedicated (commit), Renew + Private (VPC/on-prem), Expand (upsell), Non-renew (offboarding plan).
 - Recommendation: One-line rationale and ask (e.g., approve 12m renewal at committed capacity with 30% discount).
 - Speaker note: Tie recommendation to business outcomes and technical risk.

Slide 13: 90-day joint success plan (RACI)
 - Objectives (3 max), key results, owners, due dates, success signals.
 - Quick wins (30 days), mid-term (60 days), long-term (90 days).
 - Speaker note: Assign owners and get verbal buy-in in the meeting.

Slide 14: Renewal tracker (embedded table) — sample columns (text representation)
 - Columns: Account, Renewal date, Renewal window (Qx YYYY), Current ARR, Recommended path, Risk score (0-10), Primary blocker, Owner, Next action, ETA, Status
 - Example row: [Acme Corp, 2026-04-30, Q2 2026, $420k, Renew+Dedicated, 7, p99 latency spikes, Ethan Rivera, Schedule SE deep-dive, 2026-03-20, at-risk]
 - Speaker note: Use this live during the QBR to update status and owners.

Slide 15: Risk scoring rubric (how to compute)
 - Components (weighted): Business impact (40%), Technical health (30%), Adoption trajectory (20%), Contractual cues (10%).
 - Score 0-10 mapping: 0–3 = green (low risk), 4–6 = amber (medium), 7–10 = red (high risk).
 - Speaker note: Encourage a short calibration conversation when scoring.

Appendix (use as needed)
 - Appendix A: Raw metrics queries and dashboards (links to Grafana/BigQuery).
 - Appendix B: Model eval examples (before/after prompts).
 - Appendix C: Contract/terms summary and renewal clauses.

Post-QBR runbook (actions to close within 7 days)
 - 1) Update renewal tracker with final decision + assign next steps (Owner: CSM).
 - 2) If technical risk > 6: SE to run 7-day stability plan and weekly check-ins (Owner: SE).
 - 3) If cost optimization recommended: Product Ops to propose batching/quantization schedule and estimated delta (Owner: Product Ops).
 - 4) Prepare executive summary email + ask (Owner: AE).

Templates & artifacts to attach to the deck
 - One-page executive summary (for CFO/Head of Product).
 - Health export (CSV) with last 90 days of latency/errors/usage.
 - Renewal terms comparison (T+30 / T+90 options).

Checklist before running the QBR (CSM)
 - Pull last 90 day dashboards and attach to appendix.
 - Run a dry-run with SE and AE (30 min).
 - Share meeting goals and pre-read (1 pager) at least 3 business days ahead.
 - Confirm invite list includes an executive sponsor.

Notes on scaling for standard vs enterprise
 - Standard (SMB / small-mid): shorten to 45–60m, combine slides 3–6 into one Adoption & Value slide, minimal appendix, focus on quick wins and 30-day checklist.
 - Enterprise: full two-track run; add compliance deep-dive, attach contract specifics in appendix, schedule separate technical breakout if needed.

Open questions / current TODOs (internal)
 - Add a one-click export of the renewal tracker to SFDC (ask GTM ops).
 - Create a standard set of BQ queries for cost-per-inference that are parameterized by model and deployment type.
 - Automate risk-score calibration using historical renewal outcomes (R&D idea).

Draft footer: Draft v0.9 — internal CSM/SE playbook. Feedback welcome in thread: #cs-qbr-templates.
